authority: Both options are single characters, distinct from each other and from every other picture property, so this is a well-formed decimal format under XPath 3.1 F&O 4.7.1 and the picture rules apply unmodified. With "," as the decimal-separator the fractional part of the sub-picture is "##0.00", and F&O 4.7.3 says "The fractional part of a sub-picture ... must not contain an instance of the optional digit character that is followed by a member of the decimal digit family". F&O raises the single code FODF1310 for every picture-string violation; JSONata splits it into D3080-D3093, one per rule. The JSONata documentation publishes no error-code page, so what this case pins is the classification — which F&O rule the picture breaks — and the code is how jsntrs names it.
